column1: # The four Revit 2025 RE1 projects and Revit's own IFC2X3 exports of them, from Drshelden/IFC-ECS (MIT),
# the one list of what CI fetches of them (#1457). Fetched by .github/actions/fetch-re1 for Corpus
# health (tier 2), IfcOpenShell validates exports, the Python wheel job and the viewer's browser tests,
# which used to carry the same hashes four times over, with two cache keys, two fetches that cached
# nothing and a fallback host only one of them had. The action keeps all eight files in one Actions
# cache entry keyed on this file, saved on main only, checks every file's sha256 and byte count
# whether it was restored or downloaded, and downloads only a file that is missing or fails its pin,
# from the raw host and then the media host. A file that fails its pin fails the job. At this commit
# the media host answers 404 for all eight files (they are plain blobs, not Git LFS objects), so a
# fetch comes from the raw host; the media host is the fallback for a pin that moves to LFS content.
# The hashes are the pins ci.yml and viewer-test.yml carried before this file; the byte counts are
# research/witness-registry.json's, and all sixteen values were measured again from the raw host on
# 2026-11-05. research/witness-registry.json repeats these hashes for the witness gates (its URLs
# float on `main`, these are pinned to the commit); .github/workflows/ci.yml checks that the two agree.
# A new pin is an edit of the commit below and of the rows it changes, and the pull request that
# moves it runs every job that reads these files.
